questions.title: A mature ovum carries 22 autosomes and one X chromosome
questions.subject: dev
questions.question: How many chromosomes, and of what type, are normally present in a mature human ovum?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A mature ovum can never carry a Y chromosome, because oogenesis begins from an XX primary oocyte, which has no Y chromosome to segregate into any of its meiotic products.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 44 autosomes and two X chromosomes describes the full diploid complement of a primary oocyte before meiosis, not the haploid complement of the mature ovum after both meiotic divisions.
explanations.C: Correct. Meiosis halves the diploid chromosome number of 46 (44 autosomes plus the XX pair) to the haploid number of 23; since only an X chromosome is available to segregate, a mature ovum's normal complement is 22 autosomes plus one X chromosome (22,X). This is why the sperm's sex chromosome, not the egg's, ultimately determines the chromosomal sex of the resulting zygote.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This double-counts the sex chromosome contribution to the autosome total — the haploid set is 22 autosomes plus 1 sex chromosome (23 chromosomes total), not 23 autosomes plus a separate X chromosome (which would total 24).

questions.learning_objective: State that a mature human ovum normally carries 22 autosomes and exactly one X chromosome (never a Y), and explain that the fertilizing sperm therefore determines offspring sex.
